text:
maria: Heads-up — saw a burst of scale-down churn in the us-west-2 GPU nodepools after a short network flap at ~04:12. CA removed 4 nodes across two AZs, killing warm caches and causing higher latency for a handful of prod jobs.

kai: Oof. Do we know what expander and scale-down flags the CA was running with?

maria: Our CA args (snippet from the configmap):
```
args:
  - --expander=least-waste
  - --scale-down-unneeded-time=8m
  - --scale-down-unready-time=10m
  - --scale-down-delay-after-add=10m
  - --balance-similar-node-groups=true
  - --max-empty-bulk-delete=2
```

tom: least-waste + low unneeded/unready times explains it. Network flaps mark nodes NotReady briefly, CA treats them as eligible after unready-time and unneeded-time overlaps.

anita: Can we confirm whether those NotReady nodes still had GPU-backed workloads pinned (taints/tolerations)? If pods were still counted, CA should have left them.

maria: Some pods had local-device-plugin mounts and were transiently reporting terminated. The issue is CA sees lower allocatable and thinks it can binpack. Also the AZ spread made it worse — one AZ dipped and CA consolidated to the others, then back.

kai: Two quick levers we should try: bump --scale-down-unready-time to 30m for GPU pools, and increase --max-empty-bulk-delete to 4 so CA doesn't nukes multiples during noisy windows. Also consider expander=priority with locality-aware weights (penalize cross-AZ moves).

tom: Agree on priority expander. We can add node-template weights per nodepool so CA avoids migrating GPU-backed pods across AZs. Example weight config in agent: node-pool weight 100, best-effort pools 10.

anita: Another defensive option: enable warm-pool for the GPU nodepools (min-size 1-2) to keep a hot node around. Cost impact is small compared to repeated model cold starts.

maria: Cost numbers (rough): warm-pool 1x p4d node ~ $2.10/hr. The measured extra inference latency from cold nodes added ~200ms per request and increased throughput cost due to retries. Keeping 1 warm node is cheaper than the repeated 3-4 node churn we saw.

autoscaler-bot: scale-down suppressed: recent-scale-up cooldown 12m (reason: --scale-down-delay-after-add).

kai: Action items: 1) bump --scale-down-unready-time -> 30m for gpu nodepools (experimentally set), 2) switch expander to priority + add locality weights for us-west-2 pools, 3) increase max-empty-bulk-delete to 4 and scale-down-unneeded-time to 12m, 4) enable warm-pool min-size=1 for critical GPU pools, 5) add alert: CA oscillation >3 cycles in 20m.

maria: I'll open a small change PR to the CA daemonset config and roll to a canary pool (us-west-2a) first. @kai can you prepare the node-template weight mapping? I'll add the warm-pool toggle in the nodepool controller.

tom: One more: add a short-lived Prometheus rule to flag "nodes marked NotReady > 3m and then reclaimed by CA within 15m" so we can catch network-induced churn earlier.

anita: SGTM. If the canary behaves, we roll cluster-wide next week. :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks all — I'll post the PR + rollout notes here once ready.
